title: Weekly community
hookLine: a gathering: a congregation, a group, a meal
tomorrow: what did Jesus tell a crowd of worriers to go and look at?

lines: SUNDAY, WITH NO ONE TO SEE.
cards: People who leave a church, a team or a hometown sometimes say the hardest part wasn't the beliefs. It was Sunday afternoon, with no one to see.

The Buddha's attendant Ananda once came to him with a thought he'd been turning over. Lord, he said, it seems to me that good friendship, good companionship, is half of the holy life. It sounds generous.
Half! The Buddha's answer was not the one he expected.

teach.b: Not so, Ananda, the Buddha said. Don't say that. Good friendship is the whole of the holy life.
Someone with good friends, he went on, can be expected to walk the path. Then he pointed to himself. People bound to birth, aging and death are set free, he said, by relying on me as a good friend.
The word is kalyana-mitta, the good friend, the admirable friend. This is why community sits at the center of Buddhist practice, not at its edge.
Buddhists take refuge in three things, the Three Refuges: the Buddha, the Dhamma, his teaching, and the Sangha, the community that practices it.

teach.h: THE SANGHA: A THIRD OF THE REFUGE.
teach.b: The sangha isn't a bonus for people who like groups. It is one third of what Buddhists rely on. Monks and nuns live it every day; lay Buddhists meet at a temple or a meditation group, share food, chant together.
Ananda was the Buddha's own attendant, and even he thought friends were a helpful half. The Buddha said they are the whole road: with good friends, a person can be expected to walk it.
Weekly community is that teaching made regular: one gathering, the same people, again and again, until they're yours.

how: Buddhists take refuge in the Buddha, the Dhamma and the Sangha; monks and nuns live in community, and lay Buddhists gather at temples and meditation groups to chant, sit and share food.

o: a big crowd you join once in a while for the energy
a gathering you return to each week, with the same people
an online group you follow but never actually meet

games.q: the whole of the path: tap the pairs.
p: friendship is half the holy life
not so: it is the whole
the community, one of three refuges

s: Buddhist practice is mainly something you do alone on a cushion
the Buddha called good friendship the whole of the holy life, and the Sangha is one of the three refuges.
Ananda thought good friendship was half of the path
he said so, and the Buddha corrected him: it's the whole.
in the sutta, the Buddha names himself as a good friend
beings are set free, he says, by relying on him as a good friend.

games.q: your cousin quit her running club: 'i can run alone, the group was just a nice extra.' which line from the story fits?
o: good friends are the whole of the path, not a nice half.
solitude is the real path; friends mostly distract you.
friends matter only once you're already good at it.
games.why: Ananda offered half; the Buddha said the whole. Good friends are how anyone walks the path at all.

practice: Picture five chairs around you. In each, seat one person you see often enough to call your own.
If a chair stays empty, name one weekly gathering where you might find them, a congregation, a group, a class, a shared meal, and the day it meets.

wordCard.voice: Weekly community: one gathering you return to every week, the same people, the good friends the Buddha called the whole of the path.

orig.note: Pali (written in Devanagari): the good friend, the admirable friend.

carryVoice: Keep this one: my people, not half the path but the whole of it. Talk soon.

sources.ref: Samyutta Nikaya 45.2, Upaddha Sutta (Ananda: good friendship is half the holy life; the Buddha: not so, it is the whole; beings are freed by relying on him as a good friend)
